question: The plasma concentration of a drug in the steady state is:

options.opa: The range of plasma concentration achieved with a drug after five half-lives have elapsed.
options.opb: The maximum expected plasma level with a drug in chronic treatment.
options.opc: The area under the curve produced by any dose in the course of a chronic treatment.
options.opd: The molar equivalent to the elimination half-life.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Drug administration" -> "repeated dosing" -> "drug accumulation" -> "steady state" -> "plasma concentration stabilizes" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Drug dosing" -> "five half-lives" -> "steady state achieved" -> "plasma concentration range" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Chronic treatment" -> "consistent dosing" -> "steady state" -> "maximum expected plasma level" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Drug dose" -> "chronic treatment" -> "area under the curve" -> "total drug exposure" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Drug elimination" -> "half-life" -> "molar equivalent" -> "unclear relation to steady state" -> 50%
analysis: The plasma concentration of a drug in the steady state refers to the range of plasma concentration achieved when the rate of drug administration equals the rate of elimination, typically after about five half-lives. This is when the drug concentration remains consistent over time with regular dosing. Therefore, the correct option is the one that describes this range of concentration after five half-lives.
